title: What road life was really like
summary: Goines and Hawkins discuss tiredness, a late dance in Bluefield and failing brakes.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You know, when people look back, or when they take a look at your career, all they can see is, they walk by and they recognize you and they do. I mean, they, and they see your records and they see your picture and they see you in the books and all that and see only the glamour and stuff. But, you know, being on the road, when I listen to a lot of guys and them, when I remember my experiences, it isn't all that much fun some times.

I mean, it just isn't fun. I mean, it's really rough. You're just jumping on the bus and you're going some place and you're playing. Then, you're getting back on the bus sleepy cause you have to be some place else the next day or the next night and
That's right. You have, packing it, live in a bag.

We've had our tough times out there. But, you know, when you think about them, you say it's pretty rough through the years, but there were some very good experiences, the way things are today. You know, I say that kids don't know what they missed. But, I don't think they'd want to go through that. But, we had some tough times, travelling those one night stands especially if you had accidents, not accidents, just break downs. You know, going from one place to another. And then, you had those two lane roads. Now, it's a pleasure. It's a pleasure driving out there now, four lanes, you know. Going from here, I remember the time going from here to Buffalo. I think the Highway is Number 1. And, it took you from, you'd leave in the morning and you'd get there at night. You know, some time. That's how far it is. And,
So, it used to wear you out. When you get there, you're just worn out.

I remember the time that I was going somewhere in Bluefield, West Virginia. We was, people there was waiting for us for a dance. We broke down somewhere on the road. The bus broke down and I had to get cabs as quick as we could. We were supposed to be there at 8 or 9:00. We got there, maybe it was about 11. Order About, the amount of cabs we'd need for 20 people. But, the people waited. They were told we were coming and they waited. That was rough.

Those were some days going around those mountains. I remember one time that I got so scared. We was coming down one of those mountains in Bluefield, West Virginia. And the bus, you know, we didn't have that protective railing on the side. You could look down and you wouldn't see nothing. And, the brakes on

the bus kind of went. And this driver, I had to give it to him. He was going around trying to slow this bus. Now, I didn't know this. I was telling him to slow down. I didn't know the brakes were gone. But, he made it. I don't know how he did it. We could've gone over that mountain any time. I wouldn't have been here today.

I was just thinking about it when you asked me about some times, things back then. We had some rough times. But, we just laughed about it later. And, we forgot all about it, like nothing every happened. Now today and then, I think about that sometimes, you know?
